title: Unit – 1 : Session – 6 : SLO – 2 | Modular Programming
sections: 1) Program broken into reusable methods: static int readN(){ return new java.util.Scanner(System.in).nextInt(); }  static boolean isEven(int n){ return n%2==0; }  static void report(int n){ System.out.println(n + (isEven(n) ? " even" : " odd")); }

2) Main + two helpers: public class Main { static int square(int x){ return x*x; }  static void printResult(int v){ System.out.println("Result: " + v); }  public static void main(String[] a){ printResult(square(6)); } }  Output: Result: 36.

3) Code reuse via static methods: static methods belong to the class, not instances, so any code can call ClassName.method() without creating objects — Java's Math.sqrt(), Math.pow(), Integer.parseInt() are examples; our own utility classes (e.g., a Utils class with static helpers) give the same reuse across the program.
